<summary>
This bill would change how Tennessee public charter schools are proposed, approved, renewed, and overseen. It would define an “authorizer” as a local board of education, the Tennessee Public Charter School Commission, or the Achievement School District when it makes decisions on charter applications and agreements. It would also define “replication” as creating one or more charter schools with the same academic focus as an existing school operated by the same sponsor or governing body.

A sponsor seeking to open a new charter school generally would apply to the local board, unless the law allows a direct application to the commission. Applications would use a form developed by the State Board of Education with the commission, be filed by February 1 of the year before the planned opening, and be reported by the authorizer to the commission within 10 days. The commission would have to post letters of intent it receives within 10 days. Beginning July 1, 2025, if the commission overturns a local board’s denial of an application three times within three consecutive years, sponsors seeking to open schools in that district could apply directly to the commission for the following five years. The commission would have 90 days to decide each completed application; if it did not act, the application would be approved. After a denial, the sponsor could submit a corrected application within 30 days, and the commission would have 60 days to decide it; inaction would mean approval. The commission’s decisions would be final, and an approved school would have the commission as its authorizer and local education agency. After the five-year period, applications would again go to the local board unless the three-denial condition occurs again.

A governing body could seek to replicate a school in the district where it already operates if at least one of its charter schools had operated for a full school year when it submitted its letter of intent. It could apply to the local board or directly to the commission. Direct commission applications would follow the same deadlines, correction process, and final-decision rules described above. Public institutions of higher education could also apply to a local board or directly to the commission. A school they sponsor could give an enrollment preference to children of the institution’s employees or governing-body members, up to 25 percent of total enrollment.

The bill would require each authorizer to report renewal applications to the commission within 10 days. If the commission approves a renewal after overturning a local board’s decision, or under specified provisions of state law, the renewed agreement would last from five to ten academic years, with the commission setting the term by resolution. A governing body could petition its authorizer to change a charter agreement or to end it voluntarily before expiration; the commission would set the timelines and appeal process for amendment requests, and its denial of an amendment could not be appealed when it is the authorizer.

The bill would require the education commissioner to prepare an annual report on charter-school enrollment, geographic distribution, and performance. By January 1 each year, each authorizer would have to submit and publish a report listing its schools’ operating status, oversight and contracted services, and performance reports. The commission would annually publish certain information described in the bill. By December 1, each local education agency collecting authorizer fees would report the previous school year’s fees and the authorizing work paid for with those fees to the State Board; the State Board would post the information by December 11. An authorizer that has not adopted a performance framework for all its schools would have to use the State Board’s model framework. The bill also shifts specified responsibilities or references from the Department of Education to the commission or State Board, repeals section 49-13-142, and changes the stated start dates in two provisions to January 1, 2021. The bill itself would take effect July 1, 2025.
</summary>

claims.claim: The commission's decisions under this direct-application route are final.
claims.summary_quote: The commission’s decisions would be final
claims.source_quote: The commission's decision is final and not subject to appeal.
claims.rationale: The finality rule is explicit.

claims.claim: The commission becomes the authorizer of a school it approves under this route.

claims.source_quote:
If the commission approves an application, then the

 commission is the authorizer and LEA for that public charter school;

claims.source_quote:
If the commission approves an application, then the

 commission is the authorizer and LEA for that public charter school;

claims.claim: LEA stands for local education agency.

claims.claim: After the five-year window, sponsors must again apply to the local board unless the qualifying reversal conditions recur.
claims.summary_quote: After the five-year period, applications would again go to the local board unless the three-denial condition occurs again.
claims.source_quote:
After the five-consecutive-year period during which a sponsor may

apply directly to the commission for approval pursuant to this subsection (h), a

sponsor that seeks to establish a new public charter school must apply directly to

the local board of education unless the conditions in subdivision (h)(1) are met in

the future.
claims.rationale: Read with the preceding description of overturned denials, this accurately states the return rule.

claims.claim: A governing body's replication application must concern the district where it already operates.
claims.summary_quote: A governing body could seek to replicate a school in the district where it already operates
claims.source_quote:
may apply for replication in the LEA in which the governing

body is currently operating
claims.rationale: The geographic restriction matches.

claims.claim: Having any charter school that has operated for a full school year at the letter-of-intent stage is sufficient for replication eligibility.
claims.summary_quote: if at least one of its charter schools had operated for a full school year when it submitted its letter of intent
claims.source_quote:
A governing body that has at least one (1) public charter school authorized

by a local board of education or by the commission that has been in operation for at

least one (1) full school year at the time the governing body submits its letter of intent
claims.rationale: The stated eligibility condition is broader than the bill's: the existing school must also be authorized by a local board or the commission.

claims.claim: An eligible replication applicant may apply to the local board or directly to the commission.
claims.summary_quote: It could apply to the local board or directly to the commission.
claims.source_quote:
may apply for replication in the LEA in which the governing

body is currently operating to the local board of education or directly to the commission.
claims.rationale: Both application routes are expressly available.

claims.claim: Direct replication applications have the same 90-day initial decision deadline described for subsection (h) applications.

approve or deny a replication application no later than ninety

If the commission fails to approve or deny a replication application

 within ninety (90) days, then the application is deemed approved;
claims.rationale: The incorporated description of the initial deadline and approval consequence matches.

claims.claim: A denied direct replication applicant has 30 days after receiving the grounds for denial to submit a corrected application.
claims.summary_quote: Direct commission applications would follow the same deadlines, correction process
claims.source_quote:
Upon receipt of the grounds for denial, the sponsor has thirty (30) days to

 submit an amended replication application to correct any deficiencies.
claims.rationale: The replication correction opportunity is the same as the process described earlier.

claims.claim: The commission has 60 days to decide an amended replication application.

Upon

 receipt of the amended application, the commission has sixty (60) days to deny

 or approve the amended application.
claims.rationale: The amended-application decision period matches the earlier description.

claims.summary_quote: Direct commission applications would follow the same deadlines, correction process, and final-decision rules described above.
claims.rationale: The incorporated inaction rule is expressly repeated for replication.

claims.summary_quote: Direct commission applications would follow the same deadlines, correction process, and final-decision rules described above.
claims.source_quote: The commission's decision is final and not subject to appeal.
claims.rationale: Section 34 repeats the finality rule.

claims.claim: Public institutions of higher education generally may apply to a local board or directly to the commission.
claims.summary_quote: Public institutions of higher education could also apply to a local board or directly to the commission.
claims.source_quote:
A public institution of higher education in this state that seeks to open

a public charter school may apply to the local board of education or directly to the

commission.
claims.rationale: The bill limits this route to public institutions of higher education in Tennessee, rather than public institutions generally.

claims.claim: Schools sponsored by public institutions of higher education generally may offer the described enrollment preference.
claims.summary_quote: A school they sponsor could give an enrollment preference
claims.source_quote:
a public charter school sponsored

by a public institution of higher education in this state may give an enrollment

preference
claims.rationale: The summary carries forward its unrestricted institutional category; the bill limits this permission to schools sponsored by public institutions in this state.

claims.claim: The permitted enrollment preference covers children of the institution's employees or governing-body members.
claims.summary_quote: to children of the institution’s employees or governing-body members
claims.source_quote:
children of the public institution of higher education's employees or

members of the institution's governing body
claims.rationale: The preference beneficiaries match.

claims.claim: The enrollment preference is capped at 25 percent of the charter school's total enrollment.
claims.summary_quote: up to 25 percent of total enrollment
claims.source_quote:
not to exceed twenty-five percent

(25%) of the public charter school's total enrollment.
claims.rationale: The cap and denominator match.

claims.claim: Each authorizer must report renewal applications to the commission within 10 days of receipt.
claims.summary_quote: The bill would require each authorizer to report renewal applications to the commission within 10 days.
claims.source_quote:
The authorizer shall report each renewal application received by the authorizer to

 the commission no later than ten (10) days from the date on which the authorizer

 received the renewal application.
claims.rationale: The actor, recipient, and deadline match.

claims.claim: A renewal approved by the commission on appeal from a local board must have a term of five to ten academic years.
claims.summary_quote: If the commission approves a renewal after overturning a local board’s decision, or under specified provisions of state law, the renewed agreement would last from five to ten academic years
claims.source_quote:
if the commission approves the renewal of a charter agreement on appeal

 from a local board of education, then the public charter school and the commission shall

 enter into a renewed charter agreement in accordance with § 49-13-110(a) for a term of

 no less than five (5) academic years, but no more than ten (10) academic years
claims.rationale: The appeal-renewal trigger and term range match.

claims.claim: Renewals approved under the other specified statutory provisions must also have terms of five to ten academic years.
claims.summary_quote: or under specified provisions of state law, the renewed agreement would last from five to ten academic years
claims.source_quote:
if the commission approves the renewal of a charter agreement in

 accordance with § 49-1-614(k)(2)(B) or § 49-1-614(k)(4), then the public charter school

 and the commission shall enter into a renewed charter agreement in accordance with §

 49-13-110(a) for a term of no less than five (5) academic years, but no more than ten

 (10) academic years
claims.rationale: The summary does not characterize the unreproduced provisions and accurately reports the term rule attached to them.

claims.claim: The commission sets these renewal terms by resolution.
claims.summary_quote: with the commission setting the term by resolution
claims.source_quote: as determined by resolution of the commission.
claims.rationale: Both renewal provisions expressly use this method.

claims.claim: A charter school's governing body may petition its authorizer to amend its charter agreement.
claims.summary_quote: A governing body could petition its authorizer to change a charter agreement
claims.source_quote:
The governing body of the public charter school may petition the authorizer

 to amend the charter agreement.
claims.rationale: The actor, permission, and petition recipient match.

claims.claim: A governing body may petition for voluntary termination before its charter agreement expires.
claims.summary_quote: or to end it voluntarily before expiration
claims.source_quote:
The governing body of a public charter school may petition the authorizer

 for voluntary termination of the charter agreement before the charter agreement expires.
claims.rationale: The summary accurately describes a petition, not unilateral termination.

claims.claim: The commission determines timelines for approval of amendment petitions.
claims.summary_quote: the commission would set the timelines
claims.source_quote:
The commission shall determine the timelines for

 approval and the appeal process.
claims.rationale: The commission is assigned this mandatory responsibility.

claims.claim: The commission determines the appeal process for amendment petitions.
claims.summary_quote: and appeal process for amendment requests
claims.source_quote:
The commission shall determine the timelines for

 approval and the appeal process.
claims.rationale: The appeal-process responsibility is explicit.

claims.claim: When the commission is the authorizer, its denial of an amendment petition cannot be appealed.
claims.summary_quote: its denial of an amendment could not be appealed when it is the authorizer
claims.source_quote:
If the authorizer is the commission, then an appeal

 shall not be made of the commission's decision to deny a petition to amend the charter

 agreement.
claims.rationale: The prohibition and its condition match.

claims.claim: The commissioner of education must prepare an annual report on public charter schools.
claims.summary_quote: The bill would require the education commissioner to prepare an annual report
claims.source_quote:
The commissioner of education shall prepare an annual report on public

 charter schools
claims.rationale: The actor and annual reporting obligation match.

claims.claim: The commissioner's annual report must include charter-school enrollment.
claims.summary_quote: on charter-school enrollment
claims.source_quote: (1) Public charter school enrollment;
claims.rationale: Enrollment is a required report component.

claims.claim: The commissioner's annual report must include charter-school geographic distribution.
claims.summary_quote: geographic distribution
claims.source_quote: (2) Geographic distribution of public charter schools;
claims.rationale: Geographic distribution is a required component.

claims.claim: The commissioner's annual report must include charter-school performance.
claims.summary_quote: and performance
claims.source_quote:
(3) Public charter school performance, as evidenced by the information

 provided pursuant to subdivision (b)(3).
claims.rationale: Performance is a required component.

claims.claim: Each authorizer must submit an annual authorizing report by January 1.
claims.summary_quote: By January 1 each year, each authorizer would have to submit
claims.source_quote:
each authorizer shall, by January 1 each year,

 submit an annual authorizing report to the state board of education
claims.rationale: The obligation and deadline match.

claims.claim: Each authorizer must publish its annual authorizing report by January 1.
claims.summary_quote: By January 1 each year, each authorizer would have to submit and publish a report
claims.source_quote:
each authorizer shall, by January 1 each year,

 submit an annual authorizing report to the state board of education and make the annual

 authorizing report available on its website.
claims.rationale: The bill requires website availability as part of the annual reporting obligation.

claims.claim: The authorizing report must list the operating status of the authorizer's approved schools.
claims.summary_quote: listing its schools’ operating status
claims.source_quote:
The operating status of the public charter schools approved by the

 authorizer
claims.rationale: Operating status is a required component.

claims.claim: The authorizing report must describe oversight and contracted services provided to its approved schools.
claims.summary_quote: oversight and contracted services
claims.source_quote:
The oversight and contracted services, if any, provided by the

 authorizer to the public charter schools approved by the authorizer;
claims.rationale: The summary accurately identifies this report component without asserting that every authorizer provides contracted services.

claims.claim: The authorizing report must include performance reports for the schools the authorizer oversees.
claims.summary_quote: and performance reports
claims.source_quote:
A performance report for each public charter school it oversees, in

 accordance with the performance framework set forth in the charter agreement.
claims.rationale: School performance reports are expressly required.

claims.claim: The commission must annually publish the information referenced in section 49-13-116(b).
claims.summary_quote: The commission would annually publish certain information described in the bill.
claims.source_quote:
The commission shall annually make the information described in this subsection

 (b) available on its website.
claims.rationale: The bill establishes the publication duty, although the referenced information itself is not reproduced.

claims.claim: LEAs collecting annual authorizer fees must report to the State Board by December 1 each year.
claims.summary_quote: By December 1, each local education agency collecting authorizer fees would report
claims.source_quote:
By December 1 of each year, each LEA that collects an annual authorizer fee

 shall report the total amount of authorizer fees collected in the previous school year and

 the authorizing obligations fulfilled using the fee to the state board of education.
claims.rationale: The reporting actor, annual deadline, and recipient match; the abbreviation expansion is assessed separately.

claims.claim: In the fee-reporting provision, LEA means local education agency.
claims.summary_quote: each local education agency collecting authorizer fees
claims.rationale: The bill does not expand LEA. This is an explanatory expansion, not a demonstrated change to the bill's legal effect.

claims.claim: The fee report must include authorizer fees collected in the previous school year.
claims.summary_quote: the previous school year’s fees
claims.source_quote: the total amount of authorizer fees collected in the previous school year
claims.rationale: The reporting period and subject match.

claims.claim: The fee report must describe authorizing obligations fulfilled using the fees.
claims.summary_quote: the authorizing work paid for with those fees
claims.source_quote: the authorizing obligations fulfilled using the fee
claims.rationale: The summary accurately paraphrases the required description.

claims.claim: The State Board must post the fee-report information by December 11 each year.
claims.summary_quote: the State Board would post the information by December 11
claims.source_quote:
shall post the

 information received from each LEA on its website by December 11 of each year.
claims.rationale: The posting requirement and deadline match.

claims.claim: An authorizer lacking a performance framework for all its schools must use the State Board's model framework.
claims.summary_quote: An authorizer that has not adopted a performance framework for all its schools would have to use the State Board’s model framework.
claims.source_quote:
If an authorizer has not adopted a performance framework for all of the

 authorizer's schools, then the authorizer must adopt the model performance

 framework developed by the state board pursuant to subsection (a).
claims.rationale: The trigger and mandatory model-framework requirement match.

claims.claim: The bill shifts some statutory references or responsibilities from the Department of Education to the commission.
claims.summary_quote: shifts specified responsibilities or references from the Department of Education to the commission
claims.source_quote:
Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-107(a), is amended by

deleting "department of education" and substituting instead "commission".
claims.rationale: The supplied amendments expressly make this substitution.

claims.claim: The bill shifts some statutory references or responsibilities from the Department of Education to the State Board.
claims.summary_quote: from the Department of Education to the commission or State Board
claims.source_quote:
Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-121(k), is amended by

deleting "department of education" and substituting instead "state board of education".
claims.rationale: The supplied amendments expressly make this substitution.

claims.claim: The bill repeals section 49-13-142.
claims.summary_quote: repeals section 49-13-142
claims.source_quote:
Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-142, is amended by deleting

the section.
claims.rationale: Deleting the section supports the repeal description.

claims.claim: The bill changes the stated starting language in section 49-13-108(b)(5) to January 1, 2021.
claims.summary_quote: changes the stated start dates in two provisions to January 1, 2021
claims.source_quote:
Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-108(b)(5), is amended by

deleting the language "Beginning immediately upon the repeal of subdivision (b)(4)" and

substituting instead the language "Beginning on January 1, 2021".
claims.rationale: This is the first of the two stated-date substitutions.

claims.claim: The bill changes the stated starting language in section 49-13-121(f) to January 1, 2021.
claims.summary_quote: changes the stated start dates in two provisions to January 1, 2021
claims.source_quote:
Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-121(f), is amended by

deleting "Beginning immediately upon the repeal of subdivision (e)" and substituting instead

"Beginning on January 1, 2021".
claims.rationale: This is the second stated-date substitution; the summary does not confuse it with the bill's effective date.

claims.claim: The bill takes effect July 1, 2025.
claims.summary_quote: The bill itself would take effect July 1, 2025.
claims.source_quote: This act takes effect July 1, 2025, the public welfare requiring it.
claims.rationale: The effective date matches exactly.
